cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and David's son, starts building the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. The spot is Mount Moriah. And friend, this isn't some random lot he found scrolling his phone at midnight.

cards.question: Solomon builds the house of the LORD on Mount Moriah. What had happened on that mountain before?

answers.text: The LORD had appeared to David there
David had been anointed king there

cards.text: Solomon breaks ground on the spot David had prepared, the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. Second day, second month, fourth year of his reign, and friend, after my years in the back of a junk drawer, I couldn't even tell you what YEAR it was.

Then the house goes up on a foundation sixty cubits long and twenty wide, and the GOLD starts: the inside of the portico, the main room paneled in cypress, the beams, the thresholds, the walls and the doors. Cherubim get carved on the walls, and precious stones go in too. Friend, the only gold I own is the base I'm standing on, and I am NOT stepping off it.

cards.question: Solomon sets precious stones in the temple, and the text says they're there for ___.

cards.text: Then comes the Most Holy Place, with six HUNDRED talents of fine gold on the inside alone. Two gold-covered cherubim stand in there on their feet, facing the main room, their wings reaching wall to wall and touching each other in the middle. Then the veil: blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven in. Friend, my apron comes in exactly one color: WHITE.

In front of the temple, he makes two pillars, thirty-five cubits high together, with chainwork on top and a hundred pomegranates fastened into it. He sets one on the south and one on the north and names them Jachin and Boaz (not the Boaz from the book of Ruth). A HUNDRED pomegranates, friend, and I get tired topping one batch.

Now the furnishings: a bronze altar ten cubits HIGH, and friend, I'd need a LADDER just to see the top. Then the Sea of cast metal, round, standing on twelve oxen and holding three thousand baths. Not the Tub. Not the Big Bowl. The SEA. He also makes ten basins for washing, five on the south side and five on the north.

cards.question: Solomon makes ten basins for washing. What gets rinsed in them?

answers.text: The parts of the burnt offering

cards.question: The ten basins are for rinsing the parts of the burnt offering. So who uses the Sea for washing?

cards.text: Then come ten gold lampstands and ten tables, set in the temple five on the south side and five on the north, plus a hundred gold bowls. He makes the courtyard of the priests and the large court, with bronze on the doors, and the Sea goes in at the southeast corner. Friend, I've had a whole planet to myself all this time and I STILL can't decide where the cooling rack goes.
Huram, a craftsman working for King Solomon, makes the pots, shovels and sprinkling bowls for the house of God.

cards.question: True or false: Huram finishes the work he took on for King Solomon in the house of God.

cards.text: The finished work: the two pillars with their network and four hundred pomegranates, the stands and basins, the Sea and its twelve oxen, the pots, shovels and meat forks. Huram-abi, the craftsman Hiram king of Tyre sent (2 Chronicles 2:13), made it all in polished bronze, cast in clay molds on the plain of the Jordan. That's one to-do list, friend, and I need a nap after ONE batch.

cards.question: Solomon makes all these bronze articles in such great abundance that the ___ of the bronze couldn't be determined.

cards.text: Then Solomon makes all the furnishings for the house of God, starting with the golden altar and the tables. From bronze to GOLD, friend, and this man does NOT do anything halfway.

cards.question: What gets placed on the tables Solomon makes for the house of God?
True or false: The lampstands of pure gold and their lamps burn out in the large court.

cards.text: Last comes more gold: flowers, lamps, tongs, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, censers, and the gold doors to the Most Holy Place and the main hall. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't done.
